Build the Julia library

Source: R/backend.R
install_backend.Rd

Compiles the Julia code of every installed package that uses jlbind into one shared library, stored in tools::R_user_dir("jlbind", "data"). Run this after you install or update one of those packages. You need Julia 1.13 or later. The first build downloads and compiles the Julia dependencies, which can take a few minutes.

Usage

install_backend(
  packages = NULL,
  julia = NULL,
  ask = interactive(),
  force = FALSE,
  update = FALSE,
  develop = NULL
)

Arguments

packages

Names of the installed packages to build. By default, every package listed by jlbind_clients(). The others aren't bound.

julia

Path to the julia executable. By default, the JULIA environment variable, or julia on the PATH.

ask

If TRUE, ask before building. Defaults to interactive().

force

If TRUE, rebuild even if the library is up to date. Always on with update or develop.

update

If TRUE, use the newest dependency versions instead of those in the packages' Manifest.toml files.

develop

Paths to local Julia packages to use instead of their released versions.

Value

The path to the library (invisibly), or NULL if there was nothing to build.

Details

All packages share one Julia environment. By default, the dependencies get the versions in the first package's Manifest.toml. If two packages conflict, the one listed later by jlbind_clients() is left out, and check_backend() says why. See vignette("jlbind") for details.

If a library is already loaded, restart R to use the new one. If the Julia used for the build is updated or removed, rebuild with force = TRUE.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
install_backend()

# With a local checkout of a Julia dependency
install_backend(develop = "~/dev/SomePackage.jl")

# Only two of the installed packages
install_backend(packages = c("pkgA", "pkgB"))
} # }
